name: InteractiveBench

intro_en: InteractiveBench evaluates active information acquisition and long-horizon decision making under a unified Horizon-T budget. The paper defines five independent testbeds: Logic, UI2Html, Math, Poker, and Trust.
scale_en: 46 logic puzzles + 50 UI screenshots + 52 math problems + 5,000 poker hands + Trust round robin
metric_en: Accuracy and solved-turn average; five-part UI score; poker winnings per hand; trust payoff per round
drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2603.04737v4. InteractiveBench formulates evaluation as a Horizon-T interaction between a player and an environment or judge, terminating on a final answer or budget exhaustion. Interactive Proofs contain three independent testbeds with hidden truth and an omniscient verifier. Logic uses 46 expert-curated Situation Puzzles filtered for interaction necessity and ambiguity resolution; the player gets at most 20 rounds of yes/no-style questions or a final explanation and receives Yes/No/Both/Irrelevant feedback. UI2Html uses 50 UI2Code-Real screenshots re-annotated by front-end experts for clarity, diversity, complexity, and feasibility; a fixed VLM summary is intentionally incomplete, each round submits full HTML plus a binary clarification, headless rendering is compared with the hidden target, and five integer sub-scores cover layout, component, style, text, and polish. Math uses 52 expert-selected HLE problems, reference derivations, a 20-round claim/final loop, four-way sparse feedback, temperature zero, and player-token budget matching against Pass@k. Interactive Games comprise no-limit Texas Holdem with 5,000 hands over ten tables and a random-horizon iterated Prisoner's Dilemma Trust Game. Logic and Math report accuracy plus average solved turns; UI2Html sums five sub-scores; Poker reports mean and standard deviation of winnings per hand plus VPIP, fold rate, and latency; Trust reports realized payoff and cooperation/betrayal statistics. Judge-scale ablations show sensitivity, so the report includes that caveat. The reviewed official repository snapshot exposes Situation Puzzle, Math, Poker, and Trust code; UI2Html is specified in the paper but was not a public repository directory at review time, so the diagram follows the paper as the authoritative five-testbed protocol.
